evidence: Derived from an attended run that stored a real key through a hidden prompt and confirmed the name by metadata-only listing.
Independent review found value-altering .env parsing, expanding read-back, signal-unsafe temp cleanup, unredacted CLI error relay, and weak argument checks; all were fixed.
Independent re-review then found an existing secret could be overwritten when the pre-store read failed; reads now stop on any error, and the reviewer confirmed the fix at the reviewed revision.
Authoring live checks found the real CLI exits 0 for a missing name; existence and read-back now parse JSON and treat the not-found placeholder as absent.

Twelve focused tests drive the real hidden prompt through a pseudo-terminal and a fake CLI: byte-for-byte tricky values, raw read flags, overwrite refusal, sign-in, classified errors without CLI text, mismatch, hangup cleanup, non-terminal refusal, and hostile arguments.
Live read-only checks against a real instance: an existing key is refused without --overwrite, and a missing name reaches the hidden-prompt guard.
limitations: Uses the person's attended Infisical login; machine identity flows are out of scope.
An uncatchable kill can leave the private temporary folder behind.
A stored value equal to the CLI not-found placeholder is indistinguishable from absence.
